title: Nursery First Term
overview: Nursery First-Term Curriculum Intent Nursery is a significant developmental progression from Crèche while remaining firmly within Early Years. Children increasingly EXPLORE -> COMMUNICATE -> PARTICIPATE -> REPRESENT -> THINK -> CONNECT -> BECOME MORE INDEPENDENT. The seven EYFS areas remain interconnected, with increasingly intentional adult-guided learning alongside sustained play, continuous provision, outdoor learning and child-initiated exploration. Crèche to Nursery Developmental Shift Crèche Nursery Progression Experience language Use increasingly varied language Communicate immediate needs Participate in longer interaction Listen to short stories Engage with and discuss stories Experience sounds/rhymes Develop phonological awareness Scribble and make marks Give increasing meaning to marks Experience quantity Develop stronger number sense Match and sort Compare, classify and explain simply Explore objects Investigate properties Play alongside others Develop cooperative play Attempt self-care Become increasingly independent Notice the environment Ask questions about the environment Explore creatively Represent experiences and ideas Follow routines Take responsibility within routines Core Nursery movement: EXPLORE -> NOTICE -> NAME -> DESCRIBE -> REPRESENT -> CONNECT Critical Nursery Literacy Principle Nursery literacy is strong but developmentally appropriate. It deliberately develops oral language, vocabulary, listening, attention, story comprehension, nursery rhymes, songs, rhythm, rhyme, alliteration, environmental sounds, voice sounds, oral blending experiences where appropriate, book knowledge, name recognition, drawing, mark-making, fine-motor development and meaningful early writing behaviours. Nursery does not race children through Reception-level phonics merely to appear academically advanced. First-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 Welcome to Nursery Belonging, routines and independence 2 All About Me Identity, language and representation 3 My Body and My Senses Body knowledge, movement and investigation 4 Keeping Myself Healthy Self-care, hygiene and healthy routines 5 My Feelings and Friendships Emotional literacy and relationships 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Responsive review 7 My Family and Home Relationships, language and belonging 8 My School and Community People, places and responsibility 9 Colours, Shapes and Patterns Around Me Mathematical noticing and representation 10 Numbers in My World Early number sense and quantity 11 Plants and Living Things Observation, growth and stewardship 12 Christmas - Love, Giving and Celebration Faith, story and creative expression 13 Look How I Have Grown Reflection, consolidation and progression Nursery First-Term Communication Spine Adults deliberately introduce useful vocabulary through sustained interaction rather than vocabulary testing. Model descriptive and reasoning language: 'You chose the long red block'; 'Your tower is taller than mine'; 'Tell me what happened to the plant'; 'I wonder why he feels sad'; 'What could we try?' Nursery First-Term Phonological Awareness Children regularly experience environmental sounds, instrumental sounds, body percussion, rhythm and rhyme, playful alliteration, voice sounds and sensitive oral blending where developmentally ready. These create strong foundations for later systematic phonics. Nursery First-Term Literacy Entitlement Every Nursery child experiences books daily: fiction, rhymes, traditional tales, Nigerian/African stories, information books, picture books, varied families and child interests. Children listen, talk, predict, join refrains, retell, role-play, sequence, draw, make marks and increasingly communicate meaning. Writing begins with meaning, not pages of copied letters. Nursery First-Term Mathematics Spine Establish strong foundations in quantity, one-to-one correspondence, cardinality, small-number recognition, subitising experiences, comparison, more/fewer, same/different, matching, sorting, shape, space, position, pattern, size and sequence. Mathematics appears throughout construction, snack, songs, outdoors, stories, tidying, role play, Practical Life and adult-guided activity. Nursery Practical Life Progression Crèche ended with LET ME TRY. Nursery develops I CAN DO MORE. Children increasingly manage belongings, carry trays, pour, transfer, wipe, sweep, wash, serve, fold, sort, open/close, fasten, restore resources, care for plants, prepare simple activities and take classroom responsibility. Practical Life supports concentration, coordination, order, independence, confidence and responsibility. Continuous Provision Provide rich accessible areas for Books & Communication, Writing/Mark-Making, Mathematics, Construction, Small World, Role Play, Creative Arts, Practical Life, Investigation, Sensorial Exploration, Fine-Motor Development and Outdoor Learning. Weekly themes should not close down children's other interests. Outdoor Curriculum Outdoor learning includes running, balancing, climbing, throwing, catching, large construction, water, sand where available, gardening, nature observation, mark-making, mathematics, role play, sound exploration and collaborative play. OUTDOORS IS A LEARNING ENVIRONMENT - NOT ONLY BREAK TIME. Christian Character Spine First Term intentionally develops Belonging, Respect, Gratitude, Responsibility, Kindness, Forgiveness, Love, Service, Patience, Perseverance, Stewardship, Joy and Giving. Faith should be evident in relationships and actions, not merely displays. Nigerian and Owo Context Nursery children encounter real names, languages, families, homes, Angel Montessori School, Owo, community occupations, foods, plants, music, stories, patterns, clothing, weather and everyday Nigerian experiences, while also being exposed appropriately to the wider world. ROOTED LOCALLY - OPEN TO THE WORLD. Inclusion and SEND Nursery expectations are ambitious without being uniform. Children may need different language support, sensory access, adult scaffolding, visual support, physical adaptations, communication methods, processing time, challenge or emotional support. Ask what barrier prevents participation. ADAPT ACCESS - DO NOT REMOVE ENTITLEMENT. Parent Partnership Useful home connections include reading, conversation, rhymes, singing, meaningful counting, sorting household objects, helping prepare meals, dressing practice, family stories, photographs, drawing, noticing numbers/signs, plant care and talking about feelings. Parents should not be pressured to reproduce school at home. First-Term Assessment Assessment remains OBSERVE -> UNDERSTAND -> PLAN -> RESPOND. Useful observations include new language, story participation, rhyme awareness, one-to-one counting, recognising small quantities, cooperative problem-solving, sustained concentration, independent self-care, new physical capability, creative representation or significant misconceptions. Record what matters; not every activity requires photographic evidence. End-of-First-Term Nursery Expectations Depending on starting point and development, children increasingly communicate richly, listen longer, converse, enjoy/discuss stories, join songs/rhymes, notice sounds/rhyme, recognise own name meaningfully, make intentional marks, understand meaningful quantities, count with developing one-to-one correspondence, compare/sort, notice pattern/shape, move with increasing coordination, develop fine-motor control, cooperate, communicate emotions, investigate living things, represent ideas creatively, take responsibility and perform familiar Practical Life routines more independently. These are developmental expectations, not pass/fail criteria. Progression Into Second Term First Term establishes I BELONG -> I COMMUNICATE -> I NOTICE -> I REPRESENT. Second Term moves towards I QUESTION -> I INVESTIGATE -> I COMPARE -> I EXPLAIN -> I SOLVE, deepening community, occupations, transport, materials, forces/movement, animals, habitats, food, growth, weather, technology, mathematical reasoning, storytelling and collaborative problem-solving. Nursery First-Term Declaration We will protect Early Years principles while challenging children to grow. We will speak with them, give them words worth learning, read every day, sing, rhyme, listen, count things that matter, investigate, compare, build, create, tell stories, encourage questions, allow mistakes and another attempt, develop friendships and self-regulation, provide real responsibilities, strengthen independence, connect learning to Owo and Nigeria, widen their world, live Christian character and observe to understand. We will not confuse worksheets with rigour or early formalisation with excellence. CONFIDENT - COMMUNICATIVE - CURIOUS - THOUGHTFUL - CREATIVE - CAPABLE - INDEPENDENT - READY TO KEEP HOW DOES THIS HELP THE CHILD FLOURISH? IN GOD WE TRUST. weeks.title: Welcome to Nursery
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children establish security while taking greater responsibility for belongings and routines.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 1 - Welcome to Nursery

items.title: Belonging, routines and independence
items.learningIntent: Children establish security while taking greater responsibility for belongings and routines.
items.learningContent:
Children establish security while taking greater responsibility for belongings and routines. Vocabulary: welcome, Nursery, teacher,
friend, choose, help, please, thank you, finished, tidy, wait, turn. Develop choice, turn-taking, personal space, help-seeking,
movement, fine-motor manipulation, daily stories, name recognition, rhymes, listening games, environmental sounds, meaningful
mark-making, natural counting, matching and positional language. Practical Life: choose, carry, complete and restore. Character:
Belonging and Respect.
items.teachingGuidance:
Vocabulary: welcome, Nursery, teacher,
friend, choose, help, please, thank you, finished, tidy, wait, turn.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 1 - Welcome to Nursery

weeks.title: All About Me
weeks.curriculumIntent: Develop detailed awareness of identity and communication about self.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 2 - All About Me

items.title: Identity, language and representation
items.learningIntent: Develop detailed awareness of identity and communication about self.
items.learningContent:
Develop detailed awareness of identity and communication about self. Vocabulary: name, age, family, like, favourite, same, different,
special. Build positive identity, preferences and confidence. Recognise own name increasingly, notice meaningful letters without
formal memorisation, create an All About Me class book, draw self and explain marks. Explore age-related quantity, height informally,
photographs and same/different. Character: Value and Respect.
items.teachingGuidance:
Recognise own name increasingly, notice meaningful letters without
formal memorisation, create an All About Me class book, draw self and explain marks.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Vocabulary: name, age, family, like, favourite, same, different,
special.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 2 - All About Me

weeks.title: My Body and My Senses
weeks.curriculumIntent: Deepen body knowledge and investigate senses.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 3 - My Body and My Senses

items.title: Body knowledge, movement and investigation
items.learningIntent: Deepen body knowledge and investigate senses.
items.learningContent:
Deepen body knowledge and investigate senses. Vocabulary includes head, shoulder, knee, elbow, wrist, ankle, eyes, ears, nose,
tongue, skin, see, hear, smell, taste, touch, smooth, rough, loud, quiet, sweet, soft, hard. Develop coordination, balance, jumping,
running, throwing/catching and finger strength. Investigate sight, sound, texture, smell and safe taste. Introduce simple body
autonomy: 'My body belongs to me.' Character: Gratitude and Respect.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 3 - My Body and My Senses

weeks.title: Keeping Myself Healthy
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children understand and participate increasingly in health routines.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 4 - Keeping Myself Healthy

items.title: Self-care, hygiene and healthy routines
items.learningIntent: Children understand and participate increasingly in health routines.
items.learningContent:
Children understand and participate increasingly in health routines. Vocabulary: healthy, wash, soap, clean, teeth, brush, food, water,
exercise, sleep, rest. Sequence simple routines, practise handwashing, self-feeding, dressing, movement and care activities. Discuss
washing, brushing teeth, water, food, sleep and movement without simplistic 'bad food' labels. Practical Life: washing, wiping,
pouring, serving, dressing and cleaning. Character: Responsibility.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 4 - Keeping Myself Healthy

weeks.title: My Feelings and Friendships
weeks.curriculumIntent: Develop emotional vocabulary and positive participation with others.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 5 - My Feelings and Friendships

items.title: Emotional literacy and relationships
items.learningIntent: Develop emotional vocabulary and positive participation with others.
items.learningContent:
Develop emotional vocabulary and positive participation with others. Vocabulary: happy, sad, angry, worried, excited, calm, friend,
share, turn, sorry, help. Recognise emotions, express needs, begin negotiating, take turns, cooperate and repair relationships with
support. Use stories, character discussion, puppets, role play, faces, music/mood and calming strategies. Character: Kindness,
Forgiveness and Friendship.
items.teachingGuidance: Use stories, character discussion, puppets, role play, faces, music/mood and calming strategies.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 5 - My Feelings and Friendships

weeks.title: Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility
weeks.notes: Responsive review rather than formal examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

items.title: Responsive review
items.learningContent:
No formal examination. Revisit routines, identity, body, senses, health, feelings, friendship, language, books, phonological
awareness, number, movement and independence. Review security, spoken language, story attention, sound/rhyme noticing,
emerging number understanding, social play, self-care and children's interests.
items.assessmentFocus:
Revisit routines, identity, body, senses, health, feelings, friendship, language, books, phonological
awareness, number, movement and independence.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility

weeks.title: My Family and Home
weeks.curriculumIntent: Use richer language to describe familiar relationships and home experiences.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 7 - My Family and Home

items.title: Relationships, language and belonging
items.learningIntent: Use richer language to describe familiar relationships and home experiences.
items.learningContent:
Use richer language to describe familiar relationships and home experiences. Vocabulary: family, parent, brother, sister, baby,
grandmother, grandfather, aunt, uncle, home, room. Use family stories, photographs where available, adult-scribed descriptions and
role-play storytelling. Explore meaningful counting, household comparison, position, different families/homes, family routines and
past/present. Practical Life: folding, wiping, table setting and sorting. Character: Love and Care.
items.teachingGuidance: Use richer language to describe familiar relationships and home experiences.
items.practicalLife: folding, wiping, table setting and sorting
items.parentHomeConnection: Use richer language to describe familiar relationships and home experiences.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 7 - My Family and Home

weeks.title: My School and Community
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children understand belonging to a community of people, places, responsibilities and relationships.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 8 - My School and Community

items.title: People, places and responsibility
items.learningIntent: Children understand belonging to a community of people, places, responsibilities and relationships.
items.learningContent:
Children understand belonging to a community of people, places, responsibilities and relationships. Vocabulary may include
community, school, teacher, cook, cleaner, driver, nurse, market, shop, road, church according to context. Explore school,
appropriate staff roles, familiar community places, environmental print, role-play writing, counting/sorting, routes and model building.
Use Angel Montessori School and suitable Owo photographs. Character: Service and Respect.
items.teachingGuidance:
Vocabulary may include
community, school, teacher, cook, cleaner, driver, nurse, market, shop, road, church according to context.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Use Angel Montessori School and suitable Owo photographs.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 8 - My School and Community

weeks.title: Colours, Shapes and Patterns Around Me
weeks.bigIdea: Colours, Shapes and Patterns Around Me
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children notice, compare, classify and represent visual/spatial relationships.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 9 - Colours, Shapes and Patterns Around Me

items.title: Mathematical noticing and representation
items.learningIntent: Children notice, compare, classify and represent visual/spatial relationships.
items.learningContent:
Children notice, compare, classify and represent visual/spatial relationships. Explore circle, triangle, square, rectangle where
appropriate, curved/straight, same/different, size, position and simple repeating patterns. Shapes appear in varied sizes, orientations,
colours and materials. Use construction, pegging, threading, drawing, environmental shape hunts, printing, fabric and collage.
Include appropriate Nigerian fabric/design patterns. Character: Order and Appreciation.
items.teachingGuidance: Use construction, pegging, threading, drawing, environmental shape hunts, printing, fabric and collage.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 9 - Colours, Shapes and Patterns Around Me

weeks.title: Numbers in My World
weeks.curriculumIntent: Develop meaningful number sense through quantities, actions and everyday experiences rather than numeral recitation.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 10 - Numbers in My World

items.title: Early number sense and quantity
items.learningIntent: Develop meaningful number sense through quantities, actions and everyday experiences rather than numeral recitation.
items.learningContent:
Develop meaningful number sense through quantities, actions and everyday experiences rather than numeral recitation. Provide
one-to-one correspondence, small quantities, object counting, cardinality, more/fewer, same amount, subitising small quantities
where appropriate and number songs/routines. Count jumps, steps, throws and practical items. If a child can chant numbers but
cannot reliably give three objects, conceptual understanding still needs development. Character: Patience and Perseverance.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 10 - Numbers in My World

weeks.title: Plants and Living Things
weeks.curriculumIntent: Observe living things more carefully and begin explaining simple changes.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 11 - Plants and Living Things

items.title: Observation, growth and stewardship
items.learningIntent: Observe living things more carefully and begin explaining simple changes.
items.learningContent:
Observe living things more carefully and begin explaining simple changes. Vocabulary: living, plant, seed, root, stem, leaf, flower,
soil, water, sunlight, grow. Plant seeds, observe, compare, ask questions and care for plants. Explore taller/shorter, more/fewer
leaves and growth sequence. Use observation drawing and adult-scribed comments. Use locally meaningful plants/crops where
practical. Character: Stewardship and Patience.
items.teachingGuidance: Use observation drawing and adult-scribed comments.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Use locally meaningful plants/crops where
practical.
items.assessmentFocus: Observe living things more carefully and begin explaining simple changes.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 11 - Plants and Living Things

weeks.title: Christmas: Love, Giving and Celebration
weeks.curriculumIntent: Encounter Christmas through Christian story, language, music, creativity, relationships and generosity.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 12 - Christmas: Love, Giving and Celebration

items.title: Faith, story and creative expression
items.learningIntent: Encounter Christmas through Christian story, language, music, creativity, relationships and generosity.
items.learningContent:
Encounter Christmas through Christian story, language, music, creativity, relationships and generosity. Vocabulary: Christmas,
Jesus, Mary, Joseph, baby, gift, love, joy, give, thankful. Share an age-appropriate Nativity story, simple sequencing, songs, role
play, counting, patterns, shape, sorting, family celebration discussion and child-led art. Character: Love, Joy, Gratitude and Giving.
items.parentHomeConnection:
Share an age-appropriate Nativity story, simple sequencing, songs, role
play, counting, patterns, shape, sorting, family celebration discussion and child-led art.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 12 - Christmas: Love, Giving and Celebration

weeks.title: Look How I Have Grown
weeks.curriculumIntent: Consolidation and reflection rather than examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 13 - Look How I Have Grown

items.title: Reflection, consolidation and progression
items.learningIntent: Consolidation and reflection rather than examination.
items.learningContent:
Consolidation and reflection rather than examination. Revisit favourite books, rhymes, stories, sound games, number experiences,
body movement, Practical Life, role play, plants, art, construction and outdoors. Review language, explanation, story engagement,
sound awareness, quantity understanding, representation, cooperative play and independence across all seven EYFS areas.
items.outdoorLearning:
Revisit favourite books, rhymes, stories, sound games, number experiences,
body movement, Practical Life, role play, plants, art, construction and outdoors.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.assessmentFocus:
Revisit favourite books, rhymes, stories, sound games, number experiences,
body movement, Practical Life, role play, plants, art, construction and outdoors.
items.sourceSection: Nursery First Term / Week 13 - Look How I Have Grown
